title: Ingest-stage vectorized normalizer + shadow-prefix cache (microkernel hints) to reduce tokenizer overhead
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: A significant portion of short-to-medium (8-512 token) requests spend CPU time in the ingest side of the runtime performing normalization and tokenization prep. This causes both increased tail latency and suboptimal GPU utilization because decode workers idle waiting for tokenization/KV hints. Goal: Reduce ingest-side per-request overhead by introducing a small, tightly-optimized vectorized normalization microkernel and a tenant-aware shadow-prefix cache of canonicalized token sequences + KV-hints to short-circuit common prompt patterns. The change should be pluggable via kernel-selection heuristics so we can route workloads to the new path only when beneficial.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end p50 latency for 8-512 token distribution reduced >= 15% in synthetic benchmarks
End-to-end throughput (requests/sec) increased >= 1.7x on representative microbenchmarks with mixed short-context traffic
Shadow-prefix cache hits avoid full tokenization and return identical token+kv-hint outputs for canonicalized inputs (compat tests pass)
Fallback to full tokenizer is automatic on mismatches and does not change model output semantics
Unit + integration tests cover ASCII fast path, UTF-8 multi-byte paths, and cache eviction races
Security: tenant isolation enforced for the shadow cache; no cross-tenant leakage
progress_updates: 2025-02-10: Initial profiling run on dedicated infra (amd64, 32-core) shows 38% of CPU cycles in normalization/token-lookup for short prompts — major contributor to p95 tail.

2025-02-11: Design review: consensus to implement a small C++ microkernel using SIMD intrinsics for normalization (NFKC-lite), plus a compact shadow-prefix cache that stores (canonicalized-string -> tokenized-bytes + KV-hints). Kernel selection will use request size, recent sequence histogram, and tenant policy.

2025-02-12: Spike: implemented proof-of-concept vectorized ASCII fast path and micro-op to produce token boundary hints. Measured 2.1x reduction in normalization CPU for ascii-heavy traffic in the spike harness.
2025-02-14: Microkernel PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1684 — includes SIMD path, UTF-8 fallback, and benchmark harness. Awaiting infra/bench signoff.

2025-02-16: Implemented tenant-aware shadow-prefix cache with LRU eviction and compact hash key (64-bit). Cache stores small token slices plus a 16-byte KV-hint blob. Local microbench: combined microkernel+cache yields 1.9x throughput, 18% p50 latency reduction on 8-128 token workload. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/bench/eng/ingest-88123

2025-02-18: Design feedback from PM/Infra: require explicit opt-in rollout flag per-dedicated-cluster and strict memory cap per-tenant. Also note potential increased GC pressure for JS-ingest paths — engineering to add binding-level tests.
notes: Tradeoffs: shadow-prefix cache reduces CPU and tokenization latency for repeated prompts, but increases memory usage and introduces eviction complexity. We chose compact storage (byte-packed tokens + small KV hint) to minimize overhead.

Kernel selection heuristics: prefer microkernel+cache for requests under 512 bytes OR historically high cache-hit tenants. For long-form text (>2048 tokens) route to legacy path to avoid microkernel overhead.

Security: cache keyed with tenant-id + canonicalized input hash. All cached values are stored in tenant-scoped memory arenas; no cross-tenant exposure allowed. Must pass security review before Private deployments.
Observability: added instrumentation points for cache hit/miss, normalization path taken, time spent in microkernel, and eviction rate. These metrics will surface in Console as per-route breakdowns.

Interplay with decode scheduling: plan to emit KV-hint earlier so decode workers can prefetch attention caches and reduce GPU idle time. Need to update decode scheduler to accept 'prewarm' events from ingest.
Fallback semantics: on any parse ambiguity or hashmap collision we conservatively fallback to full tokenizer to maintain deterministic outputs. This simplifies correctness and regression risk.
Perf delta notes: we saw the biggest gains on ASCII-heavy customer workloads with repetitive system prompts; mixed-language workloads show smaller wins but still positive net improvements.
release_plan: Canary: enable microkernel+shadow-cache behind feature flag on 3 hosted regions (low-traffic) for 2 weeks
Dedicated rollout: opt-in toggle for reserved clusters; require memory cap config per-tenant
Private: ship as opt-in binary component; include audit docs for cache isolation
Rollback: feature flag toggle and eviction cold-start mitigations (throttled refill)
